T: Stay off the dirt roads. Stay for dinner.
D: Three backpackers on an outback road trip run into a friendly bushman who turns out to be anything but.
P: Serve the snacks when the backpackers stop at the roadhouse.
S: the last roadhouse before the crater
Beef chuck braised in stock and Worcestershire for 2.5 hours, thickened, in shortcrust with a puff lid, baked at 200C for 30 minutes. Tomato sauce on top.
Self-raising flour with butter rubbed in, milk mixed in with a knife, wrapped around green sticks over coals or baked in a round at 200C for 30 minutes, with butter and golden syrup.
Road trip honey soy roasted nuts

Cashews, almonds and peanuts roasted in honey, soy, chilli and sesame until glossy and crunchy, tossed with dried mango and bagged up for the car. Heat the oven to 160C. Warm 3 tbsp honey with 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil and half a teaspoon of chilli flakes. Toss through 200g cashews, 150g almonds and 150g peanuts with 1 tbsp sesame seeds. Spread on a lined tray and roast 20 to 25 minutes, stirring twice, until golden. Cool fully on the tray, break up and mix with 100g chopped dried mango.
M: camping out under the stars at the crater
Thick beef sausages cooked slowly over low coals, turned often until browned and cooked through, onions fried on a hotplate with butter, folded into white bread with tomato sauce.
the coast at Broome where the trip begins

Barramundi fillets in a crisp lager batter, fried golden, with thick chips, lemon wedges and a homemade tartare sauce of capers, gherkin and dill. Cut 1kg potatoes into thick chips and fry at 140C for 6 minutes, drain, then again at 180C for 3 minutes. Whisk 200g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder and salt with 300ml cold lager. Dust 800g barramundi pieces in flour, dip in batter and fry at 180C for 4 to 5 minutes. Mix 150g mayonnaise with chopped capers, gherkins, dill and lemon for tartare.
W: a freezing night in the desert
Scone dough of self-raising flour, butter and milk dropped in spoonfuls into simmering golden syrup, butter, brown sugar and water, covered and cooked 20 minutes until puffed. Cream.
K: Campfire billy tea with lemon myrtle
brewed on the campfire under the stars

Strong black tea boiled in the billy with dried lemon myrtle and a gum leaf, swung to settle and sweetened with condensed milk in tin mugs. Bring 1.2 litres water to the boil in a billy or saucepan. Throw in 3 tbsp loose black tea, 1 tsp dried lemon myrtle and a clean gum leaf if you have one, then take off the heat for 2 minutes. Swing the billy or tap the side to settle the leaves. Pour into tin mugs and stir in a spoon of sweetened condensed milk to taste.

s.note: the last roadhouse before the crater
s.how: Braise 800g diced beef chuck in stock and Worcestershire for 2.5 hours until tender, then thicken and cool. Line pie tins with shortcrust, fill with the beef and top with a puff pastry lid. Bake at 200C for 30 minutes and serve with tomato sauce.

Rub 60g butter into 450g self-raising flour until crumbly. Mix in 300ml milk with a knife until it just comes together. Shape into a round, score the top and bake at 200C for 30 minutes, or wrap around green sticks over coals. Serve with butter and golden syrup.

m.note: camping out under the stars at the crater
m.how: Cook 8 thick beef sausages slowly over low coals or a barbecue, turning often until browned and cooked through. Fry 2 sliced onions in butter on the hotplate until soft and golden. Fold each sausage into a slice of white bread with onions and tomato sauce.

w.note: a freezing night in the desert
w.how: Rub 30g butter into 250g self-raising flour, then mix in 150ml milk to a soft dough. Simmer 375ml water, 2 tbsp golden syrup, 30g butter and 100g brown sugar in a wide pan. Drop in spoonfuls of dough, cover and cook for 20 minutes until puffed. Serve with cream.

d.n: Campfire billy tea with lemon myrtle
d.note: brewed on the campfire under the stars
d.how: Bring 1.2 litres water to the boil in a billy or saucepan. Throw in 3 tbsp loose black tea, 1 tsp dried lemon myrtle and a clean gum leaf if you have one, then take off the heat for 2 minutes. Swing the billy or tap the side to settle the leaves. Pour into tin mugs and stir in a spoon of sweetened condensed milk to taste.
